links.outcome: vCE performance under DWI input artifacts (perturbed/degraded inputs) at inference
links.effect: Whole-image metrics largely insensitive to artifact severity; lesion MSE rose with LI artifact percentage (rho=0.478, p=0.025, n=12 lesions). HI associations not reproduced in restricted analysis.
links.quote: In contrast, post-hoc normalized lesion MSE showed a moderate positive association with artifact percentage for LI artifacts in the vCE-clean network when restricting the analysis to lesions with only strong-artifact-affected lesions ( n = 12 cases) (Spearman ρ = 0.478, p = 0.025), noting that this analysis was based on a very small subset, as shown in Fig. 7 .

links.outcome: Performance differences between two MRI scanners (acquisition devices)
links.effect: Whole-image SSIM significantly higher on Vida than Skyra Fit (both p<0.001); e.g., vCE-clean 0.868 vs 0.825 SSIM; lesion-based performance largely consistent across scanners.
links.quote: Independent of the model, examinations acquired on the MAGNETOM Vida demonstrated significantly higher whole-image SSIM than those acquired on the MAGNETOM Skyra Fit (both p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Effect of poor-quality (artifact-laden) DWI inputs on vCE output reliability
links.effect: Severe low-intensity DWI artifacts were associated with higher lesion-based error (lesion MSE rho=0.478 in restricted analysis); authors suggest automated input quality-control step; artifact prevalence 11% severe slices.
links.quote: Furthermore, automated detection of poor DWI image quality or severe artifacts during or immediately after image acquisition and before vCE synthesis could represent a useful quality-control step within future AI-augmented (semi-)automated imaging workflows.
